lines.ruling: Ruling: representation; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 1. The project's f8889.step1_total is the sum of the monthly family amounts ($8,550 a month) for the months the filer was treated as having family coverage, before division by 12; the reply, as its note says, read the interface as the refigured line 3 (the same amount divided by 12). Triage (executable-triage-v2, .transcription/triage/2025/f8889.json): 1,553 of 1,832 agree; the completed value differences are this factor of 12 (classm.s2.4: project $8,550, reply $712.50; classm.ira.2: $102,600 v. $8,550). Both divide by 12 before line 6 (project f8889.step1_line3). Project stands. (carried over from f8889.rulings.json, matched by triage kinds and witnesses, review of 2026-11-23)

Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.hsa_split_spouse_eligible (chosen: Step 1 counts only the months both spouses were eligible individuals treated as having family coverage; p969 p. 6, Rules for married people, Caution) against the literal i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 1 that the reply follows. The project's Step 1 is read only when f8889.split holds and is zero where no spouse's Form 8889 has family months. The completed value differences (classm.s2.6.deepseek, classm.s2.7, classm.sli.4, classm.ssb.5, classm.f1040.2, classm.f8889.1: project $0, reply the filer's own amount) are returns where f8889.split is false, so line 6 is line 5 on both sides. The restructure of family_months_ok (a choose on family_same in place of an any-test) gives the same value wherever its operands are known, and these witnesses are the ones ruled before. Triage: 1,500 of 1,779 agree. Project stands.

Ruling: ambiguity; inherited from f8889.step1 (amb.2025.hsa_split_spouse_eligible; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Steps 2 and 3). Ruling: interface gap; i8889 p. 7, Line 6, Step 4. The project's f8889.step4_total is the sum of the self-only monthly amounts for the eligible months without family coverage (before division by 12); the reply read the same interface name as a line 6 total and so asks f8889.allocation on every return. Triage: 1,205 of 1,779 agree; the differences are this reading (stage11.hsa.self_full_year and stage11.hsa_excess: project $51,600, the twelve-month sum, reply $4,300, the same amount divided by 12; stage11.refuse.hsa_married and stage11.hsa.self_all_year_answer: reply $0) and the reply's unknown for want of an allocation. The project's line 6 divides by 12 where it adds Step 4. Project stands.

Ruling: ambiguity; amb.2025.hsa_split_spouse_eligible; p969 p. 6, Rules for married people, Caution ('The rules for married people apply only if both spouses are eligible individuals'); i8889 p. 7, Line 6. The reply applies the spouse rule whenever both spouses have a Form 8889 and the filer had family coverage; the project also requires the other spouse to have been treated as having family coverage at some time. Completed value differences: classm.f8889.1, fxeduhsa.hsa_spouse_never_eligible (spouse on Medicare all year) and generated returns 141, 186, 222 and 383 (one spouse's Form 8889 with no family month): project false, reply true. The other differences are the project's unknown where coverage_year or married_dec31 is not answered. Triage: 1,646 of 1,779 agree. Project stands.
